title: Unified Terraform storage module: EBS/EFS/S3 with snapshots & encryption defaults
creator: Asha Patel
description: Scope: Implement a single, composable Terraform module (redwood_storage) supporting EBS, EFS, and S3 artifacts for Private/VPC deployments. The module must: provide secure-by-default settings (encryption at rest using KMS, enforce HTTPS for S3, enable EBS encryption, enforce EFS encryption in transit when supported), opinionated snapshot lifecycle defaults (daily automated snapshots with 30-day retention, tags for owner/environment/cluster), and sane defaults for performance (EFS throughput mode decisions, EBS volume types). It should expose interfaces for customer-managed KMS keys, cross-account snapshot sharing flags, and allow opt-outs for features like versioning/MFA-delete.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Module can be consumed by private-deploy Terraform stacks to provision EBS volumes, EFS file systems, and S3 buckets with encryption defaults enabled. 2) Snapshots/backups are scheduled (AWS Backup or scheduled Lambda) by default with configurable retention. 3) Module exposes inputs for KMS key ARNs, lifecycle rules, versioning, and cross-account snapshot sharing. 4) Health-check resources (CloudWatch alarms + Systems Manager Automation documents) created to surface mount/volume/snapshot failures. 5) Documentation and migration notes for existing private deployments included.
design_decisions:
- Default to customer-managed CMKs if provided; otherwise create a module-scoped AWS KMS key with key rotation enabled.
- EBS default type: gp3 with IOPS/throughput knobs exposed; encrypt=true always.
- EFS default: GeneralPurpose throughput, default encryption at rest + recommend enable encryption in-transit; throughput_mode configurable.
- S3 defaults: Block public access, force TLS (aws_s3_bucket_policy), enable server-side encryption (SSE-KMS), enable bucket logging to central logging bucket, enable versioning by default (opt-out supported).
- Snapshots/backups handled via aws_backup_plan when available; fallback to lifecycle Lambda if customer environment blocks aws_backup APIs.
- Do not enable MFA-delete by default because it complicates automation; document manual hardening steps.
- State migration path: provide a migration script and upgrade guide for stacks using previous per-resource modules to the unified module to avoid resource replacement where possible.
tradeoffs:
- Creating module-scoped KMS keys simplifies onboarding but increases the number of keys to manage and may not satisfy some enterprise security requirements; exposed option for CMK recommended.
- Default retention of 30 days balances cost and recoverability but may be insufficient for regulated customers; retention is configurable.
- Using aws_backup_plan provides native managed backups but requires extra service permissions (may be restricted in some VPCs); include Lambda fallback.
- Enabling versioning and server access logs increases S3 costs but is critical for forensics; keep as default but document cost implications.
implementation_notes:
- Terraform structure: module root exposes submodules: ebs.tf, efs.tf, s3.tf, backups.tf, kms.tf, healthchecks.tf. Keep providers and required_version pinned.
- Outputs: resource ids/arns, kms_key_arn (if created), backup_plan_id, snapshot_ids (list), bucket_names (list).
- Use lifecycle "prevent_destroy" only when opt-in via variable to avoid accidental blocking of legitimate infra changes.
- Add deprecation warnings for old modules via README and a migration helper script (python/terraform import helpers).
